Overall I think Superpowers is useful. Brainstorming skill is great, and using subagents to adversarially review its own spec/plan catches things I would've missed. I do not like the separation of spec/plan; models are good enough to get straight to coding once the spec is written.

I personally don't like superpowers very much. My boss does. I think Claude makes more mistakes when using superpowers than when not... Just don't believe it's a silver bullet. It's still the same Claude.
IMO Superpowers isn't the ideal solution because it too lacks flexibility, but including the 'plan sketch' stage is sure an improvement [over Claude Code's native plan mode].
The install mechanism for the superpowers plugin for codex and opencode is....interesting...it's like curl|bash but with added LLM agents...

Online reviews indicate that Superpowers is best for people who are not already experienced SW development managers. For me, I am a solid KISS believer, so I have not yet found a better framework than just plain old Claude Code.
